A Psalm for the Wild-Built (cover)

The cover of Becky Chambers’s first Monk and Robot novella, a widely read work of solarpunk fiction about a tea monk and a robot.

Source
Reactor (Tor.com): Revealing A Psalm for the Wild-Built by Becky Chambers
Creator
Feifei Ruan (art) and Christine Foltzer (design)
Made
Cover revealed 22 September 2020; book published 13 July 2021 (Reactor)
Style
Solarpunk (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Gentle, hopeful, verdant
Evidence
Based on the publisher’s cover-reveal post, the Wikipedia article on the solarpunk genre, and the Wikidata edition item. The cover image was not inspected, so no visual traits are recorded.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Reactor (then Tor.com) revealed the cover on 22 September 2020 and credits “Art by Feifei Ruan; Design by Christine Foltzer”. The book was published on 13 July 2021. In the story, a tea monk meets a robot that wants to know “what do people need?”. Reactor.

Wikipedia’s solarpunk article says that in 2018 Becky Chambers agreed to write two solarpunk novellas for Tor Books, and that she published A Psalm for the Wild-Built (2021) and A Prayer for the Crown-Shy (2022). Wikipedia: Solarpunk.

Wikidata has an item for the Tor hardcover edition with a cover-artist statement. Wikidata Q107583570.

Feifei Ruan sells signed prints of the cover art. Feifei Ruan shop.

Why it belongs

The novellas are among the most widely read solarpunk fiction, so their covers are among the images most people meet first for the genre. A curator should inspect the cover before it is used as visual evidence.

What to review next

  • Inspect a large image of the cover (at least 800 px on the long side) and add observed traits.
  • Consider a record for the cover of A Prayer for the Crown-Shy (2022), after you check its cover credits on Reactor.
